title: Ramayana Set for Historic San Diego Comic-Con Debut With Ranbir Kapoor and Yash
excerpt: The film's panel in Ballroom 20 on July 23 will feature never-before-seen footage, live performances, and an AI-driven English lip-sync reveal, making it only the second Indian film to secure a major SDCC hall.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Ramayana: The Epic Begins will debut at San Diego Comic-Con on July 23 in Ballroom 20.
  • Ranbir Kapoor and Yash will join the panel alongside director Nitesh Tiwari.
  • The film features Brahma AI for English lip-sync, enhancing global accessibility.
  • Part 1 is set for a Diwali 2026 release, with music by A.R. Rahman and Hans Zimmer.
  • Ramayana is only the second Indian film to secure a major SDCC hall.
Ramayana's Comic-Con Debut
›Panel scheduled for July 23, 3:15 PM - 4:15 PM PDT.
›Ballroom 20 seats approximately 4,800 to 5,000 attendees.
›Second Indian film to secure a major SDCC hall.
›Includes never-before-seen footage and live performances.
  • Ramayana: The Epic Begins will be showcased at San Diego Comic-Con on July 23 in Ballroom 20, SDCC's second-largest venue with approximately 4,800 seats.
  • Ranbir Kapoor (Lord Ram) and Yash (Ravana) will appear alongside director Nitesh Tiwari and producer Namit Malhotra for the one-hour panel.
  • The SDCC presentation will feature an English version using Brahma AI, a new lip-sync technology developed to make the film accessible to global audiences.
  • Part 1 of the two-part saga is set for a Diwali 2026 theatrical release, with music by A.R. Rahman and Hans Zimmer.

Days after unveiling a four-minute trailer at a packed event at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi on July 18, the team behind Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana is heading to San Diego Comic-Con for what is being billed as the largest international debut for an Indian film. The panel, officially titled Ramayana: The Epic Begins, is scheduled for July 23 from 3:15 PM to 4:15 PM PDT in Ballroom 20, the convention's second-largest venue.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=PrhfmeMh14E

The SDCC appearance makes Ramayana only the second Indian film to secure a major hall at the convention, following Kalki 2898 AD. Ballroom 20, a column-free space on the upper level of the San Diego Convention Center, can seat approximately 4,800 to 5,000 attendees and has historically been reserved for major Hollywood studio presentations.

A Global Marketing Strategy

"With a reported budget exceeding ₹800 crore, Ramayana is among the most expensive Indian productions ever made."

The dual-launch approach — a domestic premiere at Bharat Mandapam followed by a global showcase at SDCC — reflects a deliberate strategy by producer Namit Malhotra and Prime Focus Studios to position the film beyond India's domestic market. According to the official SDCC listing, the panel will include "never-before-seen footage, exclusive reveals, live performances, and special giveaways."

The film's trailer, running four minutes and 15 seconds, was cleared by the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) on July 15 with a 'U' certificate, according to Bollywood Hungama. A separate version, reportedly around three and a half minutes, has been prepared specifically for the SDCC audience. The trailer is set to premiere globally on digital platforms on July 24.

Malhotra, who is also the Global CEO of the Academy Award-winning visual effects studio DNEG, will present the panel alongside director Tiwari and lead actors Ranbir Kapoor, who plays Lord Ram, and Yash, who portrays Ravana. The film's cast also includes Sai Pallavi as Sita, Sunny Deol as Hanuman, Ravie Dubey as Lakshman, Rakul Preet Singh as Surpanakha, and Kunal Kapoor as Lord Indra.

Brahma AI and the International Push

One of the panel's headline reveals will be Brahma AI, an indigenously developed artificial intelligence system designed to sync English lip movements with live-action footage, according to Sacnilk. The technology aims to solve immersion issues common in dubbed content, a move that signals the makers' intent to compete for international box office returns rather than rely solely on subtitles.

Innovative Technology for Global Reach
›Brahma AI syncs English lip movements with live-action footage.
›Aims to enhance immersion for international audiences.
›Trailer cleared by CBFC with a 'U' certificate.
›Global trailer release set for July 24.

The film's score, composed by A.R. Rahman and Hans Zimmer, further underscores the global ambitions. With a reported budget exceeding ₹800 crore, Ramayana is among the most expensive Indian productions ever made. Karan Johar has acquired the Hindi distribution rights for a reported ₹350 crore, according to Bollywood Hungama.

What It Means for Indian Cinema Abroad

For the Indian diaspora and international audiences, the SDCC panel represents a significant moment. Indian films have traditionally relied on word-of-mouth and diaspora-driven opening weekends abroad. Securing a prime slot at the world's largest pop culture convention — alongside panels from Marvel Studios and A24 — is a departure from that model.

"This is India's dream. We all have come together with one vision and one conviction — to put our story on the global platform."

— Yash, at the Ramayana trailer launch in New Delhi

The promotional campaign has also extended domestically, with a "Colours of Ramayana" art contest reaching over 400 schools across 18 Indian cities. Winners will receive early 3D trailer screenings in theatres before the public release.

Aiming for Global Impact
›Budget exceeds ₹800 crore, among India's most expensive films.
›Hindi distribution rights acquired for ₹350 crore.
›Promotional campaign reached over 400 schools in 18 cities.
›Part 1 set for Diwali 2026, Part 2 for Diwali 2027.

What's Next

The SDCC panel takes place on Wednesday, July 23 (Thursday, July 24 at 3:45 AM IST for viewers in India). Following the convention, the trailer will go live on digital platforms on July 24. Ramayana: Part 1 is set for a Diwali 2026 theatrical release, with Part 2 planned for Diwali 2027.

nri_angle: The SDCC debut positions Ramayana as a global franchise competing for international audiences, a milestone for Indian Americans and the diaspora who have long waited for Indian cinema to receive mainstream recognition at major Western pop culture events.
